newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices cooler as OPEC comes into view.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices cooler as OPEC comes into view.

text.p: Oil prices eased on Monday as traders took a cooler view of winter heating oil supply, but with OPEC unlikely to raise output at its meeting next week any losses would be slim, dealers said.
World benchmark Brent crude futures for January shed 41 cents to end at $22.89 a barrel as milder weather on both sides of the Atlantic eased fears of a shortage of heating oil.
But with stocks still severely depressed and temperatures forecast to fall again later this week, dealers were cautious about predicting an extended slide.

"People are waiting for weather forecasts and stocks data. If you can't build stocks in the next two or three weeks you're heading for a very tight market this winter," said Bo van Wijk, vice president energy risk management at Swiss bank UBS in Zurich.

U.S. stocks of heating oil, which have formed the backbone of the recent rally, are over 10 percent lower than at this time last year. Almost all of this shortfall was concentrated in the key heating oil consuming region of the northeast, the data showed.

With non-OPEC output at record levels and most OPEC producers pumping at or above their self-imposed quotas, there is little prospect of extra supply depressing prices enough to allow companies to build stocks.
A freeze of OPEC's ceiling at next week's conference would keep by far the biggest slice of unused capacity -- two million barrels per day (bpd) in Saudi Arabia -- in mothballs.
"A rollover is potentially very bullish because it means the one country with potential to help the market will keep it unused," van Wijk said.
OPEC President and United Arab Emirates Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Rakad bin Salem bin Rakad on Sunday added his voice to calls for a rollover of the 25.03 million bpd ceiling.

"The UAE will not ask for increasing its production share at the next OPEC meeting, even if it has the capability to produce more than the (current) quota," the official WAM news agency quoted Rakad as saying.

OPEC's Economic Commission Board (ECB) of market and technical experts from all 11 member states gathered on Monday in Vienna to prepare a 1997 supply-demand outlook ahead of the ministerial conference.
Despite surprisingly high oil prices, OPEC is not expected to tamper with its ceiling, OPEC delegates and ministerial sources say.

Uncertainty over winter demand and the timing of the return of Iraqi oil exports under a delayed United Nations limited oil sale plan make most OPEC members reluctant to raise the ceiling, the sources say.

In the past, the state has estimated that a daily flow of 300 million barrels is needed to keep the pipeline viable, he said. But oil-transport technology has improved significantly since then, and promises to continue improving, he said.
Alyeska is a consortium owned by oil companies with interests on Alaska's North Slope.
British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield and Exxon own major shares. Mobil, Phillips Petroleum, Unocal and Amerada Hess own minor shares.
